scope: Final bounded pass for current Saudi-market pre-company or incomplete-company-profile founders visible in 2025-2026 demo days, competitions, founder announcements or product launches. Existing worker promotions were excluded before qualification.

scoring_policy.capacity_rule: Unknown capacity stays unknown. No record receives more than one outsourcing-likelihood point without explicit evidence of external-partner intent or a documented team audit.
scoring_policy.verification_rule: Every promoted record has a confirmed person, Saudi-market basis, founder or founder-equivalent decision role, a specific software product, and at least one first-party or official source. Each B record also has a second independent source group.
scoring_policy.lane_rule: A promoted venture must still lack a complete operating-company profile; a project page or an incomplete early-stage profile does not by itself move the record out of the pre-company lane.

deduplication_audit.result: No promoted wave-three person, canonical LinkedIn URL, or known venture domain appears among earlier worker promotions.

evidence_catalog.source_title: StartSmart Saudi ninth version nominated teams
evidence_catalog.paraphrase: The official finalist roster names Yara Ali Alalawi for GreenVision and Zakaria Alezi Alnajar for Zakn, names Ghadah Alshehri for Ballora, and describes each venture's specific software product.

evidence_catalog.source_title: StartSmart Saudi announces 40 qualifying entrepreneurial ideas
evidence_catalog.paraphrase: The official program says its 2025 qualifying ideas entered an intensive Jeddah development journey with expert training, mentorship and financial prizes, and tags Marya Fawaz, Yara Alalawi and Zakn among the participants.

Fawaz identifies Ballora as her graduation project, describes representing its AI platform at King Abdulaziz University's innovation conference, and separately reports its selection for StartSmart's 2025 development program.

Alalawi calls GreenVision her project, explains how she originated it from a Saudi Environmental Fund field problem, identifies herself as its lead engineer and backend architect, and documents a cloud dashboard prototype and current next-step intent.
Alnajar's public profile lists him as Zakn founder in Riyadh and shows a current founder-controlled update placing Zakn at LEAP 2026.

The early company page describes a Saudi-market idea-and-product validation platform, links zakn.digital, shows current LEAP and StartSmart activity, and does not publish a founding year or headquarters.

An independent developer profile lists work supporting AI integration for Zakn's pre-launch product-validation platform; this corroborates active development but is not treated as a current vendor request.
The company has a public website, a Dubai headquarters, a 2-10 employee band and an identified founder, so it is an operating company rather than an incomplete-profile Saudi pre-company venture.
A matching Jeddah professional profile is visible, but its public content does not connect the person to the Haji finalist project.

context.saudi_basis: Jeddah-based creator building a system trained for invasive plant monitoring in Saudi Arabia; both the founder-controlled profile and official finalist roster state the Saudi use case.
context.founder_signal: Alalawi calls GreenVision her project, documents originating the idea from a Saudi field interview, and identifies herself as the lead engineer and backend architect.
context.software_initiative: Cloud-native environmental monitoring system combining drone imagery, localized AI classification, maps and an interactive reporting dashboard.
context.product_stage: Graduation-project prototype plus StartSmart finalist development; no standalone operating-company profile was found.
context.budget_or_traction: Official StartSmart finalist and development-program participation; no cash budget, grant amount, customer or paid pilot is claimed.
context.timing_trigger: First-party product-build and next-step updates were visible within 180 days.

lane_eligibility.reason: A named creator leads a current Saudi-market software project, while no legal entity, dedicated venture domain or complete company profile is visible.

gate_reasons.identity: The official roster names Yara Ali Alalawi for GreenVision and the exact public profile independently documents the same project.
gate_reasons.ksa_fit: The venture is designed for invasive-plant monitoring in Saudi Arabia and the creator is based in Jeddah.
gate_reasons.authority: Her first-person origin account and lead-engineer role establish a current founder-equivalent project decision role; no formal founder title is invented.
gate_reasons.software_fit: The evidenced system requires an AI pipeline, backend, cloud storage, maps and a reporting dashboard.

product_intent.reason: A specific AI, drone, backend and dashboard product was publicly described and prototyped within 12 months.

outsourcing_likelihood.reason: The creator has substantial technical capability, but the available project evidence does not establish a sufficient long-term delivery team or explicit external-builder intent; capacity remains unknown.

budget_readiness.reason: Official accelerator-style development, mentorship and prize participation are evidenced; no cash build budget is claimed.

timing.reason: Founder-controlled product-build and next-step signals were visible within 180 days.

penalties.reason: A working student prototype and individual technical capability do not by themselves establish a sufficient operating-company product and engineering team.

stopping_reason.exact_reason: Stopped after three unique B-band records cleared all four active gates and the remaining bounded finalist checks either lacked a collision-free founder-controlled identity or fell outside the pre-company lane. A fourth record was not added because the available evidence would require weakening identity, authority or lane standards.
